prompt: Complete LineCountingOutputStream, a FilterOutputStream that forwards every byte to the wrapped stream unchanged while counting how many newline bytes pass through.
explanation: FilterOutputStream is the decorator base class of the stream library: it holds the wrapped stream in a protected field called out and delegates to it, so a subclass only overrides the behaviour it wants to change. Because its inherited write(byte[], int, int) loops over write(int), overriding the single-byte method is enough for every write call to be counted. Forgetting the out.write(b) call is the classic mistake -- the counter would be right but the data would vanish.
hints: The wrapped stream is the inherited protected field out; call out.write(b) to pass the byte along.
'\n' is a char literal that compares fine against the int parameter b.
getLineCount should simply return the field you increment in write(int) -- do not recount anything.
